Next steps:

calls.name: get_survivor
calls.summary:
C4 Glucose Guide · N0072 · 61F · ovarian · ALERT
High most of the day: 63% in range, average 178 mg/dL
61-year-old female, ovarian cancer, 1.7 years after treatment; type 2 diabetes at start; group: coaching; night shift. Average sugar 178 mg/dL in weeks 1-2, 63% of readings in range. Median rise after dinner 108 mg/dL. Synthetic participant (made-up data).
Next steps:
- Only 62.7% of your readings were in the 70-180 range (weeks 1-2); the usual target is more than 70%. Your average was 178.3 mg/dL. Bring this to your next visit.
- You walked after 0 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.7 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (13.5 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.1 mg/dL less, against 20.1 for 20-29 minutes and 16.8 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, but it is not proven there yet.
- You work nights, so clock-time rules about late dinners don't fit you. Keep your main meal at the same point in your waking day.

calls.name: module_metrics
calls.summary: C1: logistic model AUROC 0.666 (95% CI 0.61-0.72), Brier 0.192, out-of-fold on 466 development survivors. Held-out status mix {"alert":41,"watch":41,"ok":117}.

structuredContent.outcome: Any ER visit or hospital stay in 2018 (outcome_acute_care_2018)

data.predictorsFrom: 2017 MEPS only (2018 file used for the outcome column only)

structuredContent.validation: 10x repeated stratified 5-fold CV on the development set, one row per survivor; OOF predictions averaged over repeats; 2000-sample patient bootstrap for 95% CIs; paired bootstrap for differences.
structuredContent.finalModel: L2 logistic regression on 34 survey-domain features + missing indicators

plainFactors.factor: ER visit or hospital stay in 2017
Fair or poor self-rated physical health

structuredContent.clinicalRecords: No meaningful gain: clinical detail (stage, comorbidities) adds nothing even inside Synthea; Synthea-derived scores give the MEPS model at most a tiny Brier gain (about -0.001) and no clear AUROC gain. But a Synthea model on shared variables alone ranks real survivors about as well as the survey model (tie within CI)
caveats: Associations, not causes. Prior acute care and poor physical function dominate; they mark need, not levers.
Small data: 466 development survivors, 134 with the outcome. Differences of a few AUROC points are within chance.
Subgroups with n < 30 or < 10 events (Hispanic, NH Asian, NH other, uninsured, colon, lung) are too small to judge.
MEPS is a US national sample; the Synthea clinical records are synthetic and resemble South Florida. Nothing from Synthea is evidence about real patients.

calls.name: module_metrics
calls.summary: C3 Radar on held-out patients: week AUC 0.819 vs schedule-only 0.808; rough-patch episode recall 0.664 vs 0.617; ER/admission recall 0.549 vs 0.434; median lead 7 days.

definition.rough_day: relative to the person: daily feeling 1, or 2+ points below their own median of the last 28 check-ins (until 5 check-ins: feeling <= 2); OR on the weekly check-in any of fatigue, nausea, pain, appetite loss, diarrhea, trouble sleeping, anxiety, sadness >= 3 or 2+ above their own usual; OR ER visit / admission / treatment paused. Skipped check-ins are not counted as rough; they are shown to the coach as a warning sign (rough rate on return rises ~1.8x after 5 skips) with a same-day wearable estimate
definition.rough_patch: a rough day followed by another within 3 days, or any clinical event; onset = first patch day after 7 quiet days
definition.forecast: each evening, P(rough patch onset in the next 7 days); days already inside a patch are not scored
definition.early_warning: an alert counts only if it fires 2+ days before onset
definition.inputs: wearable signals vs personal baseline, wear time, known treatment schedule. No self-reports, no events.
definition.split: by patient: 60% train, 15% validation (thresholds), 25% test (all numbers below)
definition.alert_budget: thresholds put 12% of quiet validation days on alert, same budget for every method

urgent.definition: P(ER visit or hospital admission in the next 7 days); urgent when in the top 3% of validation days. Separate flag; does not change the rough-patch status.

realWorld.methods:
Real-data cross-check for C4: do the synthetic patterns hold in real people?

Usage: uv run --with pandas --with numpy python -I scripts/realworld.py <dataset_dir> <out_dir>
Writes <out_dir>/realworld.json.

- CGMacros (45 real adults, minute-level Libre sensor + Fitbit): within-person effect of
  movement in the hour after a meal and of a late dinner (>= 20:00) on the post-meal rise.
  Rise = max Libre glucose 0-120 min after the meal minus the reading at the meal minute.
  Meals with another logged meal in the next 120 min are dropped. CIs: cluster bootstrap
  over people.
- NHANES 2011-2014 cancer survivors (real, one snapshot each): association of overnight
  fast, last eating hour and daily movement with HbA1c, adjusted for age and sex. Survey
  weights are NOT applied in nhanesSurvivors (describes the sample). nhanesSurvivorsWeighted applies the
  survey weights and design (strata, PSUs) and describes US adult cancer survivors 2011-2014.
